title: Taskbar does not show a normal window from a specific app (UTAU through Wine)
line: Wine apps like UTAU whose main window belongs to a hidden helper window now get their own Task Manager entry.
explanation: Wine makes the main window of apps like UTAU transient for a hidden 1x1 owner window that has skip-taskbar set. libtaskmanager hides every transient so that its leader represents it, and it also moves the active state to the topmost leader; with a skip-taskbar leader the main window had no entry at all and nothing was highlighted. The change makes a transient be represented only by its topmost leader that doesn't skip the taskbar; if there is none, the transient gets its own entry and its own active highlight, and children are updated when a leader's skip-taskbar state changes.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: show transients of windows that skip the taskbar

Some Wine apps make their main window transient for a tiny hidden owner
window that skips the taskbar, so the main window had no task entry at
all. Such transients are now shown and highlighted in their own place.

BUG: 514758

media.caption: Master: the UTAU-like main window (transient for a hidden skip-taskbar owner) is open but has no Task Manager entry
With the fix: the window has its own entry, highlighted as active
Master: after minimizing it there is no way back from the taskbar
With the fix: the minimized window keeps its entry; clicking it restores and minimizes it again

reviews.text: Representing a transient window by its topmost non-skip-taskbar leader (or itself if all leaders skip the taskbar) is a clean, principled WaylandTasksModel fix that resolves UTAU and similar Wine apps while keeping active highlighting working. However, the new effectiveWindow() semantics are not applied consistently across the rest of the class: demands-attention forwarding still targets the direct skip-taskbar parent, skipTaskbarChanged only notifies direct children rather than deeper descendants, and activeWindow is not re-synced when a leader's skip-taskbar or parent changes.
changes: Update demandsAttentionChanged (plus initial handling in addWindow and migration in parentWindowChanged) to use effectiveWindow(window) so a visible transient whose parent is skip-taskbar emits IsDemandingAttention on itself instead of forwarding to the hidden owner.
In skipTaskbarChanged, notify all descendant transients recursively (not just direct transients.keys(window)) so multi-level transient chains update their SkipTaskbar state.

When skipTaskbarChanged or parentWindowChanged changes a window's effectiveWindow() while that window or one of its transients is active, update activeWindow and emit IsActive dataChanged for the old and new effective windows.
